AcpSpec.description: An external ACP agent, such as `claude-agent-acp` or `opencode acp`.
AcpSpec.title: AcpSpec

AnswerDirectory.description: A person's answer to a session's `RequestDirectory`.
AnswerDirectory.title: AnswerDirectory

AnswerPermission.description:
A person's answer to a pending PermissionRequest: one of its options, or None to cancel it. `text`
is the person's own words: with an option, alongside the pick; alone, the whole answer, which only a
session whose agent reads answer text (the `ask_user` tool) takes.
AnswerPermission.title: AnswerPermission

ChangeDirectory.description:
Move a session to another working directory: saved in its spec, and its worker restarted there if it runs.
Refused while a turn runs. A relative `cwd` is taken from the session's current one.
ChangeDirectory.title: ChangeDirectory

ClaudeSdkSpec.description:
Claude Code driven directly over NDJSON (`claude -p`), so sessions get Remote Control.

Skeleton slice A: one process per prompt, resumed by the persisted session id. Permissions, Remote Control,
and CLI wiring arrive in later slices.
ClaudeSdkSpec.title: ClaudeSdkSpec

ClaudeTtySpec.description:
Interactive Claude Code in a pymux window: prompts are pasted in, events come from its transcript.

A person can attach to the window, and Remote Control works, which the Agent SDK behind ACP does not offer.
ClaudeTtySpec.title: ClaudeTtySpec

CompactSession.description: Summarize the session's history into a digest, outside a turn; the worker records a `compacted` lifecycle.

instructions.default: Summarize this conversation so later turns can continue the work.

CompactSession.title: CompactSession

Delivery.description: When a message reaches a session that is in a turn.
Delivery.title: Delivery

GetHistory.description:
A page of a session's history: the newest entries before `before`, the oldest after `after`, or the
newest of all when neither is given.
GetHistory.title: GetHistory

GetLive.description:
The `usertee` output the daemon still holds for a session, as a `LiveChunk`: the newest characters of the
turn it last came in. Never recorded, so gone with the daemon.
GetLive.title: GetLive

Hook.description: A pre-tool gate: when `tool` runs with rendered text matching `match`, refuse it with `message`.
Hook.title: Hook

Lifecycle.description:
Something happened to the agent's session outside a turn: interactive Claude compacted its context,
cleared it (a new agent session follows, with a Started), or ended; or the session moved directory, or changed
its sandbox.
Lifecycle.title: Lifecycle

ListAgents.description: The `aid.AgentDefinition`s on the daemon's plugins path.
ListAgents.title: ListAgents

ListModels.description:
Model providers (`aid.ModelProvider` plugins, aid's built-in ones, and models.dev's) and, for `provider`,
the models it serves. Answered from a subprocess (`python -m aid.model_lists`): the daemon imports no plugin.
ListModels.title: ListModels

LiveChunk.description:
Output an agent piped through `usertee` (`aid/usertee.py`), for a person to watch: published on its
session's live topic, and the answer to `GetLive`. `turn` is the turn it came in, None outside one. Advisory
and never recorded: a dropped chunk is gone.
LiveChunk.title: LiveChunk

MessageEntry.description: A message another session, or a person, sent to this one.
MessageEntry.title: MessageEntry

ModelCost.description: USD per million tokens. A missing cache price bills those tokens as plain input.
ModelCost.title: ModelCost

ModelEntry.description:
One model a provider serves, as its own list says, with models.dev filling what that list leaves out. None
is unknown.
ModelEntry.title: ModelEntry

NativeSpec.description:
A native agent: `agent`, the name of an `aid.AgentDefinition` on the plugins path, `target`, a
`package.module:attribute` that is an agent itself, or `instructions`, which makes the spec the agent. Exactly
one of them.
NativeSpec.title: NativeSpec

Output.description: Final event of a prompt. `output` is text for ACP and the agent's typed output for native.
Output.title: Output

PermissionMode.description: How aid answers what an agent asks permission for: an ACP agent's requests, `aid.coding`'s commands.
PermissionMode.title: PermissionMode

PermissionRequest.description:
The agent asks before a tool call, and waits for a PermissionDecision. A session whose permission mode is
`ask` waits for a person to answer it (`AnswerPermission`). A question from the `ask_user` tool is the
same shape: `tool_name` is the tool, `title` the question, `options` its alternatives (possibly none).
PermissionRequest.title: PermissionRequest

Received.description: What aid web sends the page. Only the definitions matter; this model names them.
Received.title: Received

RemoteControl.description: Claude Code's Remote Control bridge for the turn: join it in a browser or over the connect URL.
RemoteControl.title: RemoteControl

Sandbox.description:
bubblewrap around what a native session's tools start (`aid.sandbox`): the filesystem read-only but the
session's directory and `writable`, a private /tmp. A session that asks for one never runs without it: no bwrap,
or no user namespaces, and the worker refuses to start; `python`'s `in-loop` mode, which no sandbox can hold, is
refused.
Sandbox.title: Sandbox

Sent.description: What the page sends aid web.
Sent.title: Sent

SessionStatus.description: What a session is doing now, and what it runs. Never env values or MCP headers: those hold credentials.
SessionStatus.title: SessionStatus

SessionSummary.description:
A session's whole history, totalled. Token counts sum each turn's Usage, so they cover what the agents
reported and nothing more (see Usage).
SessionSummary.title: SessionSummary

SetPermissions.description:
Change a session's permission modes: `default`, the spec's `permission`, and `tools` by name (None returns a
tool to its default); every kind but claude-tty. Saved in the spec; a running worker applies them to its next
request (claude-sdk: its next prompt), while a request already waiting keeps its own.
SetPermissions.title: SetPermissions

SetSandbox.description:
Change a native session's sandbox (`NativeSpec.sandbox`; None turns it off): saved in its spec, and a
running worker restarts under it, at once when idle, else when its turn ends. Refused when bwrap cannot run
the new sandbox here.
SetSandbox.title: SetSandbox

SetSupervisor.description:
Change the session that supervises this one (`spec.supervisor`; None ends supervision): saved in its spec,
under the link's rules at creation (the supervisor exists, is not this session, closes no cycle). The worker
keeps running: the supervision plugin picks the change up from the session list.
SetSupervisor.title: SetSupervisor

SetTags.description:
Change a session's tags (`spec.tags`): each key set to its value, or removed when the value is None; tags not
named stay. Saved in its spec; the worker keeps running.
SetTags.title: SetTags

StartSession.description: Start a stopped session's worker without a turn; for interactive Claude, its pane. A running one is left be.
StartSession.title: StartSession

Started.description: A worker started, and what its backend said about itself. The daemon records one per start.
Started.title: Started

StopSession.description: Stop the worker and keep the session's state, so the next prompt starts it again.
StopSession.title: StopSession

ToolCall.description: A tool call starting, or an update to it: fields left empty keep what an earlier event of the call said.
ToolCall.title: ToolCall

TurnError.description: A prompt that ended in a Failure rather than an Output.
TurnError.title: TurnError

Usage.description:
Tokens a turn used, as its agent reports them; sent just before the turn's Output. None where the agent
says nothing.

What "the turn" covers differs by agent (measured 2026-09):
- claude-agent-acp 0.75.1: every model call of the turn, subagents included.
- opencode 1.x: the turn's last model response only.
- Native: the run, every request. `input_tokens` follows the provider: Chat Completions counts cache reads
  in it, Anthropic's Messages API does not.
- claude-tty: the main conversation's messages, each counted once; subagents write transcripts of their own,
  which aid does not read.

`context_used`/`context_size` come from the agent's own report for ACP and claude-tty. The native backend sets them
itself: `context_size` is the session's context gauge (`max_context`, half the model window by default) and
`context_used` is aid's rough estimate of the send view, since the engine reports no window of its own.
Usage.title: Usage
